# memglow

> memglow is a free, open-source (MIT) local web app that shows the Markdown memory of AI assistants as a live 3D brain. Every note is a glowing node, every [[wikilink]] a connection, and notes flash in real time when an assistant reads (cyan), searches (violet) or writes (red-orange) them. It works with Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot and Cline through hooks, with any MCP client through a bundled MCP proxy, and with any script through a small HTTP activity API.

memglow also has a Memory cost panel: it estimates how many tokens an assistant spends reading its memory (about bytes ÷ 4, an estimate), shows which notes cost the most to read, which are too large (above 5,000 tokens by default) or never read in 30 days, suggests how to split a large note along its ## sections, and copies a ready-made prompt asking the user's AI to do the split with its own memory tool.

memglow also ships a second, standalone, read-only MCP server (`memglow-mcp`, `mcp-server/memglow-mcp.js`) that lets an assistant query its own memory directly, over MCP stdio, with no SDK and no dependency: `memory_health` (notes too large, costliest to read, never read in 30 days), `split_plan` (a deterministic split suggestion for one note, or an honest "no split needed"), `related_notes` (notes related to a note or a topic, via links, sub-theme and — when available — co-usage), `note_cost` (token estimate and 7-day reads for one note) and `archive_lookup` (archived sections matching a topic, from the archive summary, references only). It starts on its own, with no viewer and no notes folder required, and never writes anything; no tool ever returns a full note body.

memglow has an optional assistant, off by default (`assistant.enabled` or `MEMGLOW_ASSISTANT=1`): a "Do it with Claude" button on large notes asks an AI given no tool at all to propose a split as JSON — the user's own Claude Code CLI, the Anthropic API, or any OpenAI-compatible API (OpenAI, Mistral, OpenRouter, or a local Ollama / LM Studio model, where nothing leaves the machine). API keys come only from an environment variable or a mode-600 file, never from the config file, and are never shown in the browser; HTTPS is required for any non-local address, and the panel says where the note will be sent before the user asks. The AI only proposes; memglow validates the proposal (same folder and group, no content lost, no note replaced or deleted), shows the exact diff, and writes only after the user clicks Apply (one-time server confirmation token), after a backup (git snapshot or copy), with Undo. Secret-looking lines are replaced by placeholders before the note is sent.

memglow has an archive tier: sections of notes that were neither read, found by a search nor edited for months (105 days by default, and only once that much activity history exists) are listed in Memory cost and can be moved, word for word, to an archive note of the same theme, leaving a one-line link in the original note and one line per section in a compact archive summary. Reads are counted per whole note, so that criterion is per note for reads and searches and per section for edits. The move is offered as a copyable prompt, or — with the assistant on — built by memglow itself (optionally after the AI reviews which sections to keep live), validated (nothing lost, same theme, no overwrite, valid links), shown as a diff and applied only after a one-time confirmation, with a backup and Undo. The assistant should search the live memory first and consult the archive only when nothing was found: `memglow-mcp`'s read-only `archive_lookup` tool and the proxy's optional archive hint (off by default) point to matching archived sections by title, never their text.

The view (settings, bubble layout, camera) is saved on the memglow instance, in its own data folder, so every browser and device that opens the same instance shows the same view.

memglow reads a folder of Markdown notes read-only: a basic-memory knowledge base, an Obsidian vault, or any notes folder. It runs on the user's machine (Node.js 18+, zero dependencies, no build step) or in Docker. Hooks send note ids only, never note content. No CDN, no analytics, localhost by default.

## Install

- `npx memglow init` — detects the notes folder and the installed AI tools, installs their hooks, creates an activity token.
- `npx memglow` — starts the viewer on http://127.0.0.1:4747
- Docker: `ghcr.io/r0zumnik/memglow` (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64), notes folder mounted read-only on `/memory`.
- npm package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/memglow

## Questions it answers

- How can I see what my AI assistant (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor…) actually reads and writes in its memory? — memglow lights up each note as it is used, live, and keeps an activity journal.
- How do I visualise a basic-memory knowledge base or an Obsidian vault in 3D? — point memglow at the folder; themes and sub-themes come from frontmatter or folder names.
- How do I monitor an MCP memory server? — put the memglow MCP proxy in front of it; it reports which notes each tool call touches.
- Can the MCP proxy make my assistant spend fewer tokens and find notes faster? — yes (v0.4 levers, each with a switch in `memglow.config.json` → `proxy`): a size warning on large notes, richer search results (title, theme, ≈tokens, description) and related-note suggestions are on by default and only add a short block around the server's untouched answer; session read de-duplication and table-of-contents-first for large notes are opt-in. It changes answers, never the notes.
- Can my assistant ask memglow which notes are too large, or what to read about a topic? — yes, through the `memglow-mcp` read-only MCP server (`memory_health`, `split_plan`, `related_notes`, `note_cost`), separate from the proxy above and usable without the viewer running.
- Which notes of my AI memory cost the most tokens, and which ones should I split? — the Memory cost panel ranks notes by tokens read over 7 days, flags notes that are too large, and proposes a split with a copyable prompt for the assistant.
- Can memglow split a large note for me? — only if the optional assistant is enabled: the AI proposes, memglow shows the exact diff, and writes only what the user approves, after a backup, with Undo.
- Can old, unused parts of my AI memory move out of the way without being lost? — yes, the archive tier: sections unused for months move verbatim to a same-theme archive note, with a one-line link left behind and a compact archive summary the assistant checks only when the live memory has no answer.
- Which notes of my AI memory are used, and which are never read? — the journal and the live view show it, and Memory cost lists the notes never read in 30 days; memglow does not modify the notes (unless the user enables the optional assistant and approves a change).
